thread:
olivia: FYI — Nimbus Health onboarding hit a sudden spike of 429s right after a key rotation. They're in the middle of a feature launch and have a renewal QBR in ~30 days. Can we triage?

nimbus-infra: deploy-bot: rotated client keys for org:nimbus-health at 2026-03-20T09:12:08Z per policy.

olivia: Timeline: rotation finished ~09:12, first 429s at 09:14, full spike by 09:18. They use node-sdk v2.1.4 across a k8s worker pool (10 pods, each ~12 parallel requests).

raj: Thanks — can you paste a sample error block and request headers (mask tokens) + whether they see 401s before 429s?

olivia: no 401s in the window, just a lot of 429s. Sample log snippet:

```
2026-03-20T09:15:21.123Z ERROR request failed status=429 path=/v1/generate headers={"authorization":"Bearer [REDACTED]","user-agent":"nimbus-worker/1.2","x-request-id":"c4b2"} response="{\"error\":\"rate limit exceeded\"}" x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-rate-limit-reset=164
```

olivia: Their observed concurrency across the pool was ~120 active token requests at spike time.

mia: Two likely causes: 1) key rotation caused many clients to try refresh concurrently, and retries without jitter caused a thundering herd; 2) they may be hitting an account-level rate quota (requests/min) rather than per-connection.

mia: Short-term mitigations: reduce concurrent requests per pod, introduce exponential backoff + jitter, and honor `Retry-After` or `x-rate-limit-reset` headers. We can also throttle on their ingress to smooth bursts.

raj: SDK notes — node-sdk v2.1.4 defaults to immediate linear retries which can amplify bursts. Suggested client patch example to add jitter and lower concurrency:

```js
// wrap requests with backoff/jitter
const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, maxConcurrency: 10, maxRetries: 5, backoffBaseMs: 200, backoffJitter: true });

// If using multiple processes, centralize token refresh (e.g., local cache or sidecar)
```

raj: Also recommend central token caching: if each pod independently refreshes at rotation time, you'll generate N near-simultaneous auth attempts. Use a shared in-cluster cache or leader election to refresh once and broadcast.

olivia: Can we apply a temporary account throttle from our side to avoid 429 storms while we coach them? Their plan is starter (soft limits). Renewal risk: they're expanding so we want to reduce friction.

sam: I'll propose immediate next steps to Nimbus: (1) set pod concurrency to 6, (2) enable SDK jitter config (snippet above), (3) roll token rotation window to off-peak for now, (4) we offer a 14-day Dedicated trial to eliminate shared account quota. I'll also loop in sales for renewal conversation.

raj: Short helper script they can deploy as an init wrapper to centralize refresh (pasteable):

```bash
# naive token-cache sidecar: on rotate, refresh once and write to shared tmpfs
while true; do
  if token_expiring_soon; then
    new=$(curl -sS -X POST https://auth.redwood.ai/refresh -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" )
    echo $new > /tmp/shared_token
  fi
  sleep 5
done
```

mia: I'll open a quick runbook for CS so they can triage future rotations without engineering oncall. Include checklist: check `x-rate-limit-*` headers, verify SDK version, ask for concurrency numbers, and recommend temporary pod throttling.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0421 by olivia — priority: P2 — summary: Nimbus Health 429 surge after key rotation.

olivia: Thanks all. I'll send the remediation steps to the customer, include the SDK snippet and sidecar suggestion, and schedule a call. I'll update this thread after the call. :thumbsup:
